mods.name: Lyrics in the Sky
mods.description: Shows synced lyrics of the song playing on your PC (Spotify, Amazon Music, browser players) word by word in the Minecraft sky. Reads the Windows media session and fetches lyrics from LRCLIB (lrclib.net) after you allow it. Not affiliated with Mojang, Spotify or Amazon.

Everything in [1.3.0-dev.21](https://github.com/Henner4746/lyrics-in-the-sky/releases/tag/v1.3.0-dev.21), plus:

## Painted skies that live with the music
16 skies of the mod's own, painted behind the lyrics in place of the game's sky: **northern lights**, a **sea of stars**, a **star nebula**, a **light show**, **fireworks**, a **thunderstorm**, an **equalizer** around the horizon, a **retro sun**, **afterglow**, **petal rain**, a **full moon**, a **ringed planet**, an **event horizon** (a black hole), a **vinyl moon**, a **pastel morning** and a **rainbow**.

- **They move with the singing:** aurora curtains, searchlights, the equalizer's bars, the black hole's disk and the record's sheen flare up on every sung word; a new line sends up fireworks or a shooting star; strong words strike lightning; a gust of wind blows the petals.
- **The moon, planet, record or sun stands where you looked** when you chose the sky, so it is in front of you.
- **Painted by the mod itself** from noise, in the background while you play – no image files, nothing taken from elsewhere.
- **Page *Himmel* (Sky)** in the menu with a picture of every sky, and settings for strength, speed, on the beat, in the lyrics' colors and night only; or `/skylyrics sky <name|off>`.
- Overworld only; with a shader pack its own sky stays.

## Tested
- In-game self tests on 26.2 and 26.3: 65 of 65 each, every sky drawn and photographed, every text in English too (0 missing). Drawing the sky takes well under a tenth of a millisecond per frame.
- 189 unit tests per version, among them: every sky looks different and is opaque, the panorama has no seam where it goes round, round shapes fade out before their edges, every sky has a picture for the menu and a name in both languages.

## English or German
The first time the menu opens (Right Shift), it asks which language the mod speaks: *Deutsch* or *English*, with the game's language as the main button. The page *Menu* and `/skylyrics language <auto|de|en>` change it later; `auto` follows the game's language. The menus, the now-playing bar, chat notes and commands, Hörgenau's notes and its introduction, and the page after the Spotify login all come in both languages.

## Presets first
The menu's start page now leads with five presets and a link to all 22, and says how much there is to set: 75 settings on 10 pages, 22 presets, 11 screen styles and 14 color palettes. A new page shows every preset as a tile with what it does, every page says how many options it has, and on the page *Display* the preset row leads to that page.

## Tested
- In-game self tests on 26.2 and 26.3: 47 of 47 each, now with photos of the language question and pages in English; every text shown in English has its English version (0 missing).
- 184 unit tests per version, among them: the English texts are in the mod, English is used when chosen or when the game speaks another language than German, numbers are written the way each language writes them, and every name and preset in the menus has its English.

Everything in [1.3.0-dev.19](https://github.com/Henner4746/lyrics-in-the-sky/releases/tag/v1.3.0-dev.19), plus:

## Hörgenau hears a new song from its start
In a game on Windows the lookup of a new song took 12 s, Hörgenau began at 9 s, and the song's start was never heard. Now a new song is listened to from its start while it is still looked up. Once the lookup is done, the recording goes on as the song's part to learn or as its sync check – or it is dropped at once when the song needs nothing. It stays in memory, ends after a minute at the latest if the lookup fails, and never starts for a livestream.

## The title's spelling
Words heard almost like a word of the song's title or artist take that spelling: in one song Whisper wrote the title's main word one letter off 28 times. Only distinctive words count, one letter off (two for long words); other forms of a word (a shorter or longer form of a title word) stay as heard. Giving Whisper the title as a prompt was tried first and did not help: with the mod's settings the prompt is not used at all, and with more context Whisper misspelled the word more often.

## Test runs skip the game's welcome screen
In a fresh run folder the game opens on its welcome screen, which held the test world back on a new Windows PC; the test runs now switch it off. Only the developer's test runs are affected.

## Tested
- **A real game** (Minecraft 26.2 with this build, Spotify playing a song lrclib.net has no text of): `listens to '…' from 0 s while it is looked up`, then `from its start (no text known)` once the music catalog answered 10 s later; learned in 93 s with its first word at 0.087 s (before: 10.3 s), 258 words in 53 lines, the title word spelled right 33 times and wrongly none. A song whose sync check was still due: the early recording became the check, `heard from its start`.
- **Windows 11** (dev.19, in a virtual machine with the Windows media player): Hörgenau recorded only the player, learned a song nobody has the text of, moved a song 0.83 s that was shown late, and found another one fitting.
- 179 unit tests per version, among them: a song is heard from its start while it is looked up, and dropped when it needs nothing; words heard almost like the title take its spelling, other forms do not. In-game self tests on 26.2 and 26.3: 37 of 37 each.

## Hörgenau on Linux
- It records the music app's own PulseAudio stream (PipeWire's PulseAudio server works too) with `parec` from `pulseaudio-utils`, found by the app's MPRIS name. A player may open its stream a few seconds after it says it plays, so it is looked for a moment; without it, all the default output plays.
- whisper.cpp has no build for Linux: build it yourself and put `whisper-cli` with its libraries into `config/lyricsinthesky/hoergenau/bin`. The model is downloaded and checked as on Windows.
- The one-time introduction stays on Windows, where one click sets everything up.

## Lines that read in the sky
What Hörgenau writes down for a song nobody has the text of came in Whisper's groups – 20 words and more in one line, which showed as a cloud of words. Now they are lines of at most eight words, broken after a comma or a full stop, else at the longest pause; every word keeps its own time.

## Tested
- **A real game on Linux** (Minecraft 26.2 with this build, the official Spotify client playing into PulseAudio, all on one machine): for a song lrclib.net has no text of, the music catalog said "a song", Hörgenau recorded only Spotify's stream (`records only spotify (stream 2)`), from 0 s to the end, and learned it in 88 s – 276 words with their times in 60 lines of 3 to 8 words – and shared it; played again, it ran word by word in the sky. For "In the End" with Deezer's word times the sync check paired 89 words and found them shown 12 ms after they are sung ("fits"); the measurement went to the tracker and counted at once.
- 176 unit tests per version, among them: a long group Whisper heard becomes lines that read; the player's stream is found by its MPRIS name. In-game self tests on 26.2 and 26.3: 37 of 37 each.

Everything in [1.3.0-dev.17](https://github.com/Henner4746/lyrics-in-the-sky/releases/tag/v1.3.0-dev.17), plus:

## Hörgenau writes down only songs
In a real game a Twitch stream played in the browser. A livestream has no length, so the check "heard 80 % of the song" never ran, and Hörgenau kept 20 seconds of what the streamer said as the stream's "lyrics". Now a song nobody has the text of is heard only
- with a song's length, 30 seconds to 20 minutes, and
- when Deezer's or Apple's music catalog know a song of that artist with that title.

Livestreams, videos and podcasts are never written down. The tracker on henrik.click checks the same before it takes such lyrics from anyone.

## Music before streams
With a Twitch stream in the browser and Spotify playing beside it, the mod followed the stream – the media session Windows called current – and Hörgenau never heard the music. Now
- a livestream is never taken as the song playing,
- a music app (Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, Deezer, Tidal and others) goes before a browser or video player,
- a stream beside the music no longer keeps Hörgenau waiting while it records only the music app's own sound.

## What Hörgenau measured counts for everyone at once
A sync check goes to the tracker as a measurement – the correction, or that the lyrics fit, with how many words were paired and how close they lay – and applies to every player right away, as long as other measurements do not contradict it. Until now it was shared like a correction set by hand and applied only once 10 players agreed. Corrections set by hand still need that.

## Always asks the tracker
Corrections and songs other players learned are fetched also with sharing switched off; the switches only decide what is sent.

## Tested
- **In the real game on Windows** (Minecraft 26.2, a Twitch stream playing in the browser): Hörgenau logged `does not listen to '…': no song (no length, a livestream)`. The new choice of the media session, run on the same PC with the stream playing and Spotify beside it, took Spotify.
- **The music catalogs, live:** five songs, two of them songs nobody has the text of, were found as songs; the titles of three Twitch streams were not.
- **The tracker, live on henrik.click:** one measurement counted for everyone at once (−240 ms); one from only 4 words paired was refused. 31 tests, also on the server's Python 3.10.
- 174 unit tests per version; in-game self tests on 26.2 and 26.3: 37 of 37 each.
